clue.text: This compiler's left to provide meaning

parts.note: the setter speaking of themself: 'this compiler is' gives I'M
port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: A setter says their own departure is meant to convey significance.
explanation.definitionFit: The import of a remark is its significance or sense, so the noun is a synonym.

clue.text: Thinks male takes liberties

parts.note: uses, as in exploits someone, takes liberties with them

explanation.surface: A man presumes too much in his thoughts.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to ponder or reflect, so muses means thinks.

clue.text: Pardons laughter, somewhat, getting offensive

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone excuses mirth that is turning rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting offensive' reads as becoming rude, but offensive here is a noun: an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: An onslaught is a fierce attack, a military offensive.

clue.text: Topic of article covering Middle East

indicators.note: in a down clue covering puts the article above the next piece

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: The subject of a newspaper piece reporting on the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject or main idea of a talk or piece of writing.

clue.text: Star's first with generous model

indicators.note: first here takes only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of Star's
ample means generous, plentiful

explanation.surface: A film star's first big break comes with a lavishly proportioned fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: A sample is a specimen or example that represents the whole, as a model does.

clue.text: Crew on board in vessel

indicators.note: on, with board, puts the crew between the two letters of the ship abbreviation

parts.note: on board conventionally means inside SS
a crew is a team
in means fashionable, as is hip

explanation.surface: Sailors aboard inside a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is a crossword convention for going between S and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamship is a ship driven by steam, a sea-going vessel.

clue.text: Mass over sacred relic's producing signs

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the mass letter on top

parts.note: M is the physics abbreviation for mass
the Ark of the Covenant is a sacred relic; ark's is its possessive

explanation.surface: A church service held over a holy relic yields omens.
explanation.definitionFit: Marks are signs or symbols, such as traces or indications.

clue.text: Car, until changed, contains black oil

indicators.note: contains means the rearranged letters hold the black letter
changed means these letters are altered into a different order

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A car needs dark engine oil until it is serviced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges the eight letters into LURICANT before 'contains' takes in the black letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil is the commonest lubricant, used to reduce friction in engines.

clue.text: Sharpens head of tool being blunt

parts.note: hones means sharpens a blade

indicators.note: head of takes the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: first letter of tool

explanation.surface: Someone sharpens a tool whose tip has gone dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blunt' reads as dull-edged, beside sharpening, but means plain-spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Being blunt means being frank and outspoken, which an honest person is.

clue.text: Meadow grazed covered in greenery

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or grassland
grazed, of animals, means fed

explanation.surface: Cattle grazed a meadow thick with vegetation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something leafed has leaves on it, so it is covered in foliage.

clue.text: Bakes without opening ovens

indicators.note: the word for bakes loses its opening letter

parts.note: roasts means bakes, cooks in an oven

explanation.surface: Someone cooks without first opening the oven door.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast is a kiln for drying hops, common in Kent; the plural is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Oasts are kilns, a kind of oven used for drying hops.

clue.text: Shocking former sweetheart, guy hugs Romeo

parts.note: ex means former
the heart (middle letter) of sweet

indicators.note: hugs means the cable wraps round the Romeo letter

parts.note: a guy is a rope or cable steadying a tent or mast
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An old flame's new man is clinging to a Romeo, which is appalling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' looks like the partner of 'former', but it is only the middle letter of sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Execrable means extremely bad, the kind of thing that shocks or appals.

clue.text: Warne ran sneakily back taking catch

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
taking means the words hold the answer within them, carried across their breaks

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Shane Warne, the Australian cricketer, sneaks back to take a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft made 'taking catch' the definition and left the hiding unsignalled; 'taking' is the containment signal and 'catch' alone is the definition. 'back' says to read the concealed run right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnare is to trap, so it fits 'catch' as a verb.

clue.text: Old lady's pet dog

parts.note: old lady is slang for mother, MA, here with 's
a pet is a sulk or petty quarrel, a tiff

explanation.surface: An elderly woman's beloved pet dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' reads as a noun for an animal, but here it is a fit of pique.
explanation.definitionFit: A mastiff is a large, powerful breed of guard dog.

clue.text: Free help with great paper

indicators.note: free means the letters are let loose to settle in a new order

explanation.surface: An offer of free assistance alongside a quality newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter names their own newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Daily Telegraph is a British national newspaper, a paper in everyday speech.

clue.text: Get allies upset and pass law

indicators.note: upset means the letters are tipped over into a new order

explanation.surface: Annoy your partners and then push a bill through.
explanation.definitionFit: To legislate is to make laws, so passing a law is the same action.

clue.text: Sense a battle over European cape

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts what comes before above the next pieces

parts.note: war means battle
ness is a headland or cape, as in Scottish place names

explanation.surface: Feeling a fight brewing over a headland in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Awareness is perception or consciousness, a sense of something.

clue.text: Splinter could be small and stiff

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
hard means stiff, rigid

explanation.surface: A splinter might be tiny and rigid.
explanation.definitionFit: A shard is a sharp broken fragment of glass or pottery, a splinter.

clue.text: Unusually green site is plain

indicators.note: unusually means the letters are arranged in an odd way

explanation.surface: An oddly verdant place is a grassland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' looks like an adjective for the site, but it is the noun: flat open land.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is a vast grassland plain in Tanzania and Kenya.

clue.text: Big inlet getting high tides, initially

definitions.text: Big inlet getting high tides, initially

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: A broad bay where high tides come in.
explanation.definitionFit: A bight is a wide curving bay or coastal recess, a large inlet of the sea.

clue.text: Bough with top of bough spread

indicators.note: top of takes the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: first letter of bough
a spread is an American term for a farm or ranch

explanation.surface: A tree limb with its tip extended outward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' looks like a verb, but in American use a spread is a large farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A bough is a main limb of a tree, which is a branch.

clue.text: Airborne soldier in suitable American gear

indicators.note: in puts the soldier inside the word for suitable

parts.note: apt means suitable
a para is a paratrooper

explanation.surface: A paratrooper kitted out in proper American equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparatus is equipment or kit for a purpose, the same as gear.

clue.text: Glow surrounds religion's first holy place

indicators.note: surrounds means the glow wraps round the opening letter

parts.note: shine means glow

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of religion's

explanation.surface: A radiance encircles faith's foremost sacred site.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrine is a place of worship hallowed by a saint or relic.

clue.text: Calm, like wise person around university

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of

indicators.note: around means the sage goes round the university letter

parts.note: a sage is a wise person

explanation.surface: Serene, like an academic sage strolling about campus.
explanation.definitionFit: To assuage is to soothe or ease, so it means calm as a verb.

clue.text: Stop state visit, finally

parts.note: aver means state, declare

indicators.note: finally picks out the end letter of the word before it

parts.note: last letter of visit

explanation.surface: A head of state calls off an official trip at the last minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state visit' reads as a diplomatic trip; state is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert something is to prevent or ward it off, so to stop it.

clue.text: Humorist is better having small heart

indicators.note: having, with heart, says the gambler holds something in his middle
heart marks where the small letter goes: the middle of the gambler

parts.note: a better is someone who bets, a punter
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A comedian proves superior by having little compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as 'superior' but is one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A punster makes puns, a kind of joker or wit.

clue.text: Alarm seeing lavatory bowl almost frozen

parts.note: a pan is a toilet bowl in British usage

indicators.note: almost means the word for frozen loses its final letter

parts.note: icy means frozen

explanation.surface: Fright at finding the toilet nearly iced over.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the pan is the bowl of a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden overwhelming fear, the same as alarm.

clue.text: Child with nearly everything is perfect

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: nearly means the word for everything loses its final letter

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A child who has almost everything is flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: Total means complete or absolute, as in a perfect stranger or total disaster.

clue.text: Clean home bothered fickle person

indicators.note: bothered means the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone flighty is irritated about tidying their house.
explanation.definitionFit: A chameleon changes colour, so figuratively it is someone who changes opinions or allegiances readily.

clue.text: Finished public school, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means we hear the school name spoken

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school, a private boarding school

explanation.surface: A boy completed his time at an elite school, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a public school is a fee-paying private school.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is eaten is consumed, all finished up.

clue.text: Oddly deep patches?

indicators.note: Oddly takes the first, third, fifth and further odd-placed letters

explanation.surface: Puzzling over strangely deep areas.
explanation.definitionFit: The depths are the deepest parts of water or ground, regions that are deep.

clue.text: Distant country it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the country's name is heard spoken

parts.note: Chile is a South American country

explanation.surface: A far-off land, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: Distant looks geographic but means cold in manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A chilly manner is cool and unfriendly, aloof, so it means distant.
